reasoning_summary: Step-by-step check of the reduction Hamiltonian Path <=p LongPath17. Lines 0002-0005: statement of the problem plus NP membership (a vertex list is a polynomial-time-checkable certificate) - correct. Lines 0006-0010: Hamiltonian Path is NP-complete (Karp) - a legitimate starting point. Lines 0011-0018: construction G = H plus 17 isolated vertices, EG = EH; computable in polynomial (indeed linear) time, and |VG| = n + 17, so the LongPath17 target is |VG| - 17 = n. Correct and well defined. Lines 0020-0028 (=>): a Hamiltonian path of H is a valid path in G since EH subset EG, and it visits exactly n = |VG| - 17 vertices. Correct. Lines 0029-0044 (<=): a simple path PG in G visiting exactly n vertices can use only edges of EH, so no isolated u_i can appear on it once the path has more than one vertex; hence all n visited vertices lie in VH, and since |VH| = n the path covers every vertex of H exactly once, i.e. is a Hamiltonian path of H (lines 0045-0049). Correct. Lines 0050-0054: both directions plus polynomial-time computability give a valid Karp reduction, so LongPath17 is NP-hard (and NP-complete). Correct. Only blemish: line 0040 asserts n > 1 without justification; for n = 1 the length-0 path could sit on an isolated vertex. This does not break the reduction, since a 1-vertex H always has a Hamiltonian path, so the equivalence still holds in that degenerate case. No step fails.
